prompt:
Let $f(x)=xe^{-x}$ for $x\ge0$.

**(a)** Find $\displaystyle\int f(x)\,dx$.

**(b)** Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty f(x)\,dx$, or show that it diverges.

**(c)** Find the area of the region bounded by the graph of $f$, the $x$-axis and the line $x=2$.

rubric.description: (a) Applies $\int u\,dv=uv-\int v\,du$ to get $-xe^{-x}+\int e^{-x}dx$
(b) Evaluates the antiderivative at $b$ and at 0
(b) Shows $be^{-b}\to0$ and $e^{-b}\to0$, and concludes the value is 1

sampleResponse:
(a) With $u=x$, $dv=e^{-x}dx$: $\int xe^{-x}dx=-xe^{-x}+\int e^{-x}dx=-xe^{-x}-e^{-x}+C$.
(b) $\int_0^\infty xe^{-x}dx=\lim_{b\to\infty}\left[-xe^{-x}-e^{-x}\right]_0^b=\lim_{b\to\infty}\left(-be^{-b}-e^{-b}\right)-(0-1)=0+1=1$, since $be^{-b}\to0$ and $e^{-b}\to0$.
(c) $f(x)\ge0$ on $[0,2]$, so the area is $\int_0^2xe^{-x}dx=\left[-xe^{-x}-e^{-x}\right]_0^2=-2e^{-2}-e^{-2}+1=1-3e^{-2}\approx0.594$.

prompt:
Let $g(x)=\dfrac{1}{x^2-x-2}$.

**(a)** Find constants $A$ and $B$ such that $g(x)=\dfrac{A}{x-2}+\dfrac{B}{x+1}$.

**(b)** Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_3^\infty g(x)\,dx$, or show that it diverges.

**(c)** Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^1g(x)\,dx$.

rubric.description: (b) Evaluates the limit (the term at $b$ tends to 0 after combining the logarithms)
(c) Uses the same antiderivative with limits 0 and 1 (no discontinuity on $[0,1]$)

sampleResponse:
(a) $1=A(x+1)+B(x-2)$. At $x=2$: $A=\frac13$. At $x=-1$: $B=-\frac13$.
(b) $\int g\,dx=\frac13\ln\left|\frac{x-2}{x+1}\right|+C$. Then $\int_3^\infty g\,dx=\lim_{b\to\infty}\frac13\ln\frac{b-2}{b+1}-\frac13\ln\frac14=0+\frac13\ln4=\frac23\ln2\approx0.462$.
(c) $g$ is continuous on $[0,1]$, so $\int_0^1g\,dx=\frac13\ln\left|\frac{1-2}{1+1}\right|-\frac13\ln\left|\frac{0-2}{0+1}\right|=\frac13\ln\frac12-\frac13\ln2=-\frac23\ln2\approx-0.462$.
